units.translation: 1149-50. αἱ μέν τ’ Αἰγαίου: The Aegaean is a river near Corcyra; its daughter is Melite, and her son by Heracles is Hyllus, from whom come the Illyrian tribe and the Hyllian harbor (1125) among the Phaeacians. Panyasis (fr. 17 Kinkel) says that Heracles, when ill in Lydia, received healing from the river Hyllus, which is in Lydia; for this reason his two sons were named Hyllus. Meliteion is a mountain of Corcyra.

1153-54. κεῖνο τὸ Μάκριδος: that which is now called the sanctuary of Medea. Timaeus (fr. 8 M. I 195) says the marriage took place in Corcyra, Dionysius of Miletus in the second book of his Argonautica (32 fr. 3 J.) says in Byzantium, and Antimachus in his Lyde (fr. 11 B. II 291) says they had intercourse in Colchis near the river.
1160. προμολὰς: he has called the places outside the cave προμολαί. Lᵐ P
1170a. 〈φαέεσσιν:〉 instead of "with lights"; for the air, being naturally dark, he made bright with lights. Lᵐ
b. It is written φαρέεσσιν. F

1174-75a. ἀνὰ πτόλιν: the city of the Corcyraeans lies on a peninsula. He says, then, in historical fashion, that they were far from the city on the shore of the peninsula on which the city is situated, as Apollonides says in his Periplus of Europe (M. IV 309). Lᵐ (P)

b. χερνήσοιο: he has called the peninsula χέρνησος, as in Book 1 (925). The peninsula opposite Corcyra he has called Macridian, perhaps because the Euboeans settled there; Euboea was formerly called Macris. Those who inhabited it after the capture of Troy 〈...〉 the Abantes 〈...〉 founded Amantia (Call. fr. 259 Schn.).
1187. ἄλλοι δ’ ἀμφιφο〈ρῆας〉: Theopompus (115 fr. 405 J.) says that what some call μετρηταί are called ἀμφιφορεῖς, and Lysanias says that the ἀμφορεύς is called ἀμφορεύς by the Athenians.
b. λιγνύς: the smoky exhalation; or the tip of the flame, which is better.
1193. εἴδεα καὶ μορφάς: Apollonius has properly used εἶδος for the face, and μορφή for the shape (Eur. Bacch. 4): "having changed his form from god to mortal."
1210. συνήμονας: companions, comrades, from συνῆσθαι (to be together). Lᴳ (P)
